plan.reviewNote: Because the available options lack dedicated outdoor gear specialists, we must rely on general activewear publishers. Among these, the urban, tech-adjacent audience in cold-weather regions represents the most viable segment for high-end technical apparel.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed a typical single order value of $650 based on the starting price for shells.
Assumed target gender is 'any' since technical ski wear is designed for all genders.
Assumed a one-time purchase model for technical outerwear.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells ultra-premium, high-performance technical ski outerwear starting at $650 to serious backcountry skiers and outdoor professionals.

publishers.rationale: Cloudfoot reaches active, high-income urban professionals who invest in premium activewear and value sustainability, matching the premium demographic willing to pay $650+ for a lifetime shell.
Movewell has a fitness-engaged audience that heavily invests in premium activewear and apparel, representing a high-AOV customer segment suitable for top-tier outerwear.
Studiogrid targets affluent, active individuals who spend heavily on wellness and fitness, aligning with backcountry skiers who treat physical activity as a lifestyle.

excluded.reason: Swiftcart focuses on fast, high-frequency convenience and grocery deliveries, which does not match the research-heavy, high-consideration purchase cycle of a $650+ ski shell.
Marlowe & Co. caters to older, affluent women looking for casual and workwear apparel, which lacks alignment with extreme backcountry skiing.
Linden Park is focused on conservative, classic workwear and apparel for mature women, which is not suitable for high-performance outdoor gear.
Everbody specializes in inclusive-size daily wear, workwear, and intimates rather than technical, high-performance athletic outerwear.
Pawline is a premium pet food and supplies subscription platform and does not align with active outdoor sports apparel.
Pantrygood is focused on organic groceries and wellness nutrition, which has no direct relevance to premium skiing hardware and technical outerwear.
Ruffco has a broad, national demographic searching for pet care products, which lacks the high-income, performance-driven niche focus needed.
Heartfoot specializes in basic apparel like socks and underwear, lacking the technical narrative required for premium ski gear.
Northbed focuses on high-end bedding and home textiles, which does not attract consumers looking for outdoor winter sports gear.
Daily Form is a science-forward vitamin and supplement DTC platform, which is irrelevant to high-end ski apparel.
Velvetline targets Gen Z beauty and minimalist skincare consumers, who are too young and budget-incongruent for $650+ technical outerwear.
Hearthstone Goods is a kitchenware brand; while high-income, its audience has no active correlation to backcountry snowsports.
Kitchenly is a high-volume meal-kit subscription platform that does not capture the highly specific performance-apparel intent required.
Stride & Stem specializes in professional footwear and machine-washable daily flats, failing to capture the extreme winter utility segment.
Tailcrate specializes in dog toys and pet treats, which does not reach the technical athletic audience.
Strandlab is dedicated to personalized DTC hair care, offering no contextual alignment for skiing.
Pop & Sip is a beverage company that focuses on gut health and functional drinks, completely unrelated to premium technical outerwear.
